```markdown
# Harbour Museum audio guide

## Intent
A visitor scans a code beside an exhibit and hears a two-minute story about it,
in English or Welsh. Volunteers record the stories on their phones and must be
able to add or replace a recording without asking anyone technical.

Why: not yet stated by the museum. (Open question.)

## Scale
- 60 exhibits, each with an English and a Welsh story (about 120 recordings).
- About 10 new exhibits a year.
- Recordings are about two minutes, made on volunteers' phones.

## Goals
- Scanning the code plays that exhibit's story with no app to install.
- The visitor picks a language once and the guide remembers it.
- Volunteers add or replace a recording themselves.
- Each upload is cleaned up automatically before it goes live: volume levelled
  to a consistent loudness and silences trimmed, so stories heard one after
  another sound alike.

## Non-goals
- A native app.
- Visitor accounts, tracking, or analytics beyond what the site already has.
- Editing tools for volunteers; they re-record and re-upload instead.

## Anti-goals
- A volunteer needs a developer to publish or fix a recording.
- Loudness jumps between exhibits.
- A visitor is asked to choose a language at every exhibit.

## Constraints
- Builds on the museum's existing Eleventy site, deployed to Netlify.
- Visitors use their own phones, often on patchy museum wifi or mobile data.
- Volunteers upload whatever their phone produces (m4a, mp3, wav, etc.).

## Approaches
Considered for handling recordings:
1. Play each phone recording as uploaded. Simplest, but phone recordings vary a
   lot in loudness and visitors hear them back to back.
2. Clean up each upload automatically (level the volume, trim silences) before
   it goes live.

Picked: 2, by the museum, for consistent sound across exhibits.

## How it works (calls made by the designer, open to correction)
- **The guide is part of the existing site**: one page per exhibit at
  `/guide/<exhibit-id>/`. The code beside each exhibit links to its page. The
  page shows the exhibit name and a player, and starts the story on a tap.
  Why: a phone camera opens a link directly; no app, and it reuses the site.
- **Language**: chosen on first visit, stored on the visitor's phone
  (browser storage), with a switch on every page. If the chosen language's
  recording is missing, the page says so and offers the other language.
- **Volunteer uploads**: a page behind a volunteer login where they pick the
  exhibit and language and upload the file from their phone. Uploading a new
  file for an exhibit and language replaces the old one; the previous version
  is kept so it can be restored.
- **Clean-up**: each upload is converted to a web-friendly compressed format,
  levelled to one fixed loudness target suited to phone speakers and
  earphones, and trimmed of silence at the start and end. Pauses inside the
  story are left alone, since they are part of how it is told.
- **Going live**: the cleaned recording publishes automatically; the
  volunteer can play it back on the upload page afterwards.
- **Adding an exhibit**: a volunteer (or staff) adds the exhibit name and gets
  its code to print.

## Left to the builder
- The login and upload tool, and where the audio files are stored (keeping
  ~120+ audio files out of the site's git history is preferred).
- Where the clean-up runs (on upload, or as a build step).
- Exact loudness target, audio format and bitrate.
- Code format and printable layout.
```

This is a project-sized piece of work, so I'm writing a full design document. A draft is at `specs/harbour-audio-guide.md`, and a reviewer is reading it now as if they had to build from it. I may come back once with a few questions before I hand it over.

A few calls I made along the way, so you can correct them:

- **The guide lives on your existing website.** Each exhibit gets its own page, and the code beside the exhibit links to it. Visitors don't install an app.
- **Volunteers get a simple upload page with a login.** They pick the exhibit and language, then upload the file from their phone. A new upload replaces the old one, and the previous version is kept in case it needs restoring.
- **Only the silence at the start and end gets trimmed.** Pauses inside a story stay, because they're part of how it's told.
- **Cleaned recordings go live straight away.** Volunteers can play theirs back afterwards.
- **If a Welsh recording is missing,** the page says so and offers the English one, and the same the other way round.
